newsitem.title: PANAMA: Strike ends at Panamanian banana plants.
newsitem.headline: Strike ends at Panamanian banana plants.

text.p: Striking workers at banana plantations run by Chiriqui Land Co, Panama's subsidiary of Chiquita Brands International Inc of the United States,
ended a 10-day stoppage on Friday and went back to work.
"The strike ended today. The union agreed to a new payment system and to look for a reduction in personnel," assistant Vice President Jorge Solergibert told Reuters by telephone.

The company will lay off about 30 percent of the packing station labor force and pay them severance pay, Solergibert said. The company agreed to rehire 65 workers that were fired during the strike that affected plantations on the Atlantic coast.

Workers were protesting against proposed lay-offs due to upgrade projects. Chiriqui Land said the modernizations are needed to to gain better access to the European market and make the plantations environmentally-friendly.

Panama lost about 50,000 18.5-kg boxes in exports each day, or some $3 million, Solergibert said. Chiriqui accounts for about 85 percent of Panama's banana exports and employs a total 11,000 people, nearly half of them on the Atlantic coast.
